"
Índios
" is a song composed by
Renato Russo
, released in 1986 on the
Dois
album by
Legião Urbana
and also released as the third single from the album in December the same year. A live version was also released in 2001 as a single from the live album
Como é Que Se Diz Eu te Amo
.
The song's title includes quotation marks, alluding to
David Bowie
's "
"Heroes"
".
[
1
]
According to Russo, they are used to indicate that the title does not refer to Brazil's first inhabitants, but to the innocence instilled in the country's people since its beginnings, with them always being fooled by their leaders.
[
2
]
The song begs for a different world, with less selfish people.
[
3
]
History and structure
Russo struggled to match the lyrics to the music. Over ten different recordings were attempted. When he was about to give up, producer Mayrton Bahia and sound technician Amaro Moço started editing the recordings, a technique they had already used a lot with the band's previous record,
Legião Urbana
.
[
4
]
The song is based on a keyboard mantra. Guitarist
Dado Villa-Lobos
only adds an acoustic guitar.
[
4
]
Reception
Reception to the song has been in general positive. Antônio Carlos Miguel, in a review of
Dois
for
Jornal da Tarde
, considered the song the album's "most fascinating" one. He said: "In a hypnotic take, repeating the same musical theme, he [Russo] attempts to translate the first and real owners of Brazil's despair (...) Works such as this one, uniting pleasure and awareness, could even contribute to the thriving of the last indigenous people. Or show the so-called civilized people that we can still learn a lot with the innocence of these peoples".
[
5
]
Gilmar Eitelwein, in a review for
Zero Hora
, said that "Índios' lyrics are very good" and, when describing another track, "Andrea Doria", said it too "attacks human falsehood found around every corner".
[
6
]
During the album's tour, amidst a performance at Caiçara Music Hall, the audience asked the band to play the song, but they refused, in spite of the public's protests.
[
7
]
